$comment: Where the shipped font subsets come from, pinned and checksummed.
Until now fonts-src/ held the previously-shipped subsets themselves, which
made the provenance circular: the source of the bytes was the bytes. Nobody
could verify that what a fold binary embeds is really IBM Plex Sans and
Geist Mono, in a repo whose whole vendoring discipline is built on being
able to verify exactly that.
These are release assets from the upstream projects, pinned by tag and by
sha256. scripts/subset-fonts.py refuses to run if a download does not match.
Bump a version deliberately, in its own commit, and re-run the script.
Google Fonts' `latin` subset, which is what the previously-shipped files
covered (232 and 225 codepoints). Kept identical so this change is about
provenance and not about which glyphs an operator gets.
U+0304, U+0308 and U+0329 are combining marks the range carries for
composed forms; U+FFFD is the replacement character, which a console
rendering upstream-controlled strings genuinely needs.
One deliberate widening: U+2191,U+2193 becomes U+2190-2193, so the
left and right arrows are covered too. The console renders them in
docs links, the back link, and — the one that matters — as the
direction prefix on every line of the wire log. Outside the subset they
came from whatever the system happened to fall back to, which in a
monospace pane means an arrow that does not match the column it starts.
